title: Telling stories & real conversation
goal: Tell a story with natural connectors, use relative clauses (the man who…, when…, where…), report what people said, and sprinkle in fillers and idioms like a native speaker.
intro:
You've got the grammar — now it's about sounding natural. Real Marathi conversation is full of little words that glue it together: **मग** (so, then), **म्हणजे** (I mean), **बरं** (well, OK), **ना** (right?), and the hearsay particle **म्हणे** ('apparently').

This unit also covers Marathi's **correlative** relative clauses — जो… तो…, जेव्हा… तेव्हा…, जिथे… तिथे… — and how to report what someone said. And you'll learn a few much-loved म्हणी (proverbs) to surprise your Marathi friends.

vocab.note: Stories often start: एकदा काय झालं… 'Once, what happened was…'
f जी, n जे, pl जे / ज्या; oblique ज्या-: ज्याने, ज्याला
असं म्हणाला 'said this'; असं का? 'why so?'

vocab.en: that is; I mean; so (you mean)

vocab.note: Hearsay marker at the end of a clause.
To a woman: अगं aga. Respectful: अहो.
f · गंमत म्हणजे… 'the funny thing is…'
m · मुद्द्याचं बोला 'get to the point'
Dative: मला कळलं 'I understood / I found out'

phrases.en: Meaning what? / What do you mean?
What can I say! / You won't believe it!
Honestly? (lit. shall I tell the truth?)

phrases.native: तो म्हणाला की तो येणार नाही.
phrases.roman: to mhaṇālā kī to yeṇār nāhī.
phrases.en: He said that he wouldn't come.
So what else is new? (to a man)
Stop pestering me! (lit. don't eat my head)
I'm starving. (lit. crows are cawing in my stomach)
It takes two to tango. (lit. one hand can't clap)
A bad workman blames his tools. (lit. can't dance, so the courtyard is crooked)

grammar.title: Relative clauses: जो… तो…, जेव्हा… तेव्हा…
grammar.body:
Marathi builds 'the man who…' sentences with a **pair** of words: a relative word in the first clause and a matching demonstrative in the second.

**जो… तो** 'the one who… he': जो माणूस आला, तो माझा मामा आहे 'The man who came is my uncle.' (f: जी… ती; n: जे… ते)
**जे… ते** 'what… that': जे झालं ते झालं 'what's done is done'
**जेव्हा… तेव्हा** 'when… then': जेव्हा मी पोहोचलो, तेव्हा सगळे झोपले होते
**जिथे… तिथे** 'where… there': जिथे तू राहतोस, तिथे खूप झाडं आहेत
**जसं… तसं** 'as… so'

In everyday speech these are often replaced by a **participle** before the noun: मी वाचलेलं पुस्तक 'the book I read', काल आलेला माणूस 'the man who came yesterday'.

examples.native: जो मुलगा तिथे उभा आहे, तो माझा भाऊ आहे.
examples.roman: dzo mulgā tithe ubhā āhe, to mādzhā bhāū āhe.
examples.en: The boy who is standing there is my brother.

examples.native: जी साडी मी घेतली, ती खूप महाग होती.
examples.roman: jī sāḍī mī ghetlī, tī khūp mahāg hotī.
examples.en: The sari that I bought was very expensive.

examples.native: जेव्हा मी लहान होतो, तेव्हा आम्ही गावी राहायचो.
examples.roman: jevhā mī lahān hoto, tevhā āmhī gāvī rāhāytso.
examples.en: When I was small, we used to live in the village.

examples.native: जिथे चांगला वडापाव मिळतो, तिथे गर्दी असते.
examples.roman: jithe tsāṅglā vaḍāpāv miḷto, tithe gardī aste.
examples.en: Wherever you get good vada pav, there's a crowd.

examples.native: मी काल पाहिलेला सिनेमा छान होता.
examples.roman: mī kāl pāhilelā sinemā chhān hotā.
examples.en: The film I saw yesterday was good.

grammar.title: Reporting speech: म्हणाला की…, असं म्हणाला, म्हणे
grammar.body:
**With की:** X म्हणाला / म्हणाली की + what was said. Marathi often keeps the original wording (like a direct quote) without shifting tense: तो म्हणाला की मी उद्या येईन 'He said (that) he'd come tomorrow' (lit. 'I will come').

**Quote + असं म्हणाला / म्हणून सांगितलं:** 'मी येईन' असं तो म्हणाला.

**Questions:** X ने विचारलं की + question: तिने विचारलं की तू कधी येणार? 'She asked when you're coming.'

**Hearsay:** add **म्हणे** at the end: तो आजारी आहे म्हणे 'Apparently he's ill.'

Note: म्हणणे in the past is used intransitively (तो म्हणाला, ती म्हणाली) or ergatively (त्याने म्हटलं) — both are common.

examples.native: ती म्हणाली की तिला बरं वाटत नाही.
examples.roman: tī mhaṇālī kī tilā baraṃ vāṭat nāhī.
examples.en: She said she isn't feeling well.

examples.native: आईने विचारलं की तू जेवलास का.
examples.roman: āīne vichārlaṃ kī tū jevlās kā.

examples.native: त्यांनी सांगितलं की ऑफिस उद्या बंद आहे.
examples.roman: tyānnī sāṅgitlaṃ kī ôfis udyā band āhe.
examples.en: They said the office is closed tomorrow.
Apparently the banks are closed tomorrow.

grammar.title: Story glue: connectors and fillers
grammar.body:
**Sequencing a story:** एकदा (once) → मग (then) → तेव्हा (at that point) → त्यानंतर (after that) → अचानक (suddenly) → शेवटी (in the end). A classic opener: **एकदा काय झालं…** 'So once, what happened was…'

**Fillers you'll hear constantly:**
**म्हणजे** — 'I mean…, like…'
**बरं** — 'well…, OK…'; also 'got it'
**ना** — tag 'right?': आपण उद्या भेटतोय ना?
**अरे / अगं / अहो** — to grab attention or express surprise
**हं** — 'mm-hmm, I'm listening'
**काय म्हणतात ते** — 'what do you call it' (when searching for a word)
**-च** — emphasis on any word: मीच 'I myself', आजच 'today itself'

**Reactions:** बापरे! (wow / oh no!) · अरेरे! (oh dear) · खरंच? (really?) · कमाल आहे! (amazing!) · हो ना! (exactly!)

examples.native: एकदा काय झालं, मी बसमध्ये झोपलो.
examples.roman: ekdā kāy dzhālaṃ, mī basmadhye dzhoplo.
examples.en: So once, what happened was, I fell asleep on the bus.
I mean, I didn't mean it like that.
I was just about to call you myself.

dialogue.title: The monkey of Matheran
dialogue.setting: Ketan tells his friend Manasi a story from a trip to the hill station of Matheran, near Mumbai.

lines.speaker: Ketan
lines.en: Did I tell you the Matheran story?

lines.speaker: Ketan
lines.native: एकदा आम्ही सगळे मित्र माथेरानला गेलो होतो.
lines.roman: ekdā āmhī sagḷe mitra mātherānlā gelo hoto.
lines.en: Once all of us friends had gone to Matheran.

lines.speaker: Ketan
lines.native: आम्ही जिथे बसलो होतो, तिथे खूप माकडं होती.
lines.roman: āmhī jithe baslo hoto, tithe khūp mākḍaṃ hotī.
lines.en: Where we were sitting, there were lots of monkeys.

lines.speaker: Ketan
lines.native: मग अचानक एक माकड आलं आणि राहुलचा वडापाव घेऊन पळालं!
lines.roman: mag achānak ek mākaḍ ālaṃ āṇi rāhultsā vaḍāpāv gheūn paḷālaṃ!
lines.en: Then suddenly a monkey came and ran off with Rahul's vada pav!

lines.speaker: Manasi
lines.native: अरे देवा! मग राहुलने काय केलं?
lines.roman: are devā! mag rāhulne kāy kelaṃ?
lines.en: Oh God! So what did Rahul do?

lines.speaker: Ketan
lines.native: तो माकडाच्या मागे पळाला, आणि त्याचा चष्मा पण पडला!
lines.roman: to mākaḍāchyā māge paḷālā, āṇi tyātsā chaṣmā paṇ paḍlā!
lines.en: He ran after the monkey, and his glasses fell off too!

lines.speaker: Manasi
lines.en: Poor guy! What happened in the end?

lines.speaker: Ketan
lines.native: शेवटी जो माणूस तिथे शेंगदाणे विकत होता, त्याने माकडाला शेंगदाणे दिले आणि चष्मा परत मिळवला.
lines.roman: shevaṭī dzo māṇūs tithe sheṅgdāṇe vikat hotā, tyāne mākḍālā sheṅgdāṇe dile āṇi chaṣmā parat miḷavlā.
lines.en: In the end, the man who was selling peanuts there gave the monkey some peanuts and got the glasses back.

lines.speaker: Manasi
lines.native: म्हणजे वडापाव गेला, पण चष्मा वाचला!
lines.roman: mhaṇje vaḍāpāv gelā, paṇ chaṣmā vātslā!
lines.en: So the vada pav was gone, but the glasses were saved!

lines.speaker: Ketan
lines.native: हो ना! राहुल म्हणतो, 'मी परत कधीच माथेरानला जाणार नाही!'
lines.roman: ho nā! rāhul mhaṇto, 'mī parat kadhīts mātherānlā dzāṇār nāhī!'
lines.en: Exactly! Rahul says, 'I'm never going to Matheran again!'

culture: Marathi has a rich store of **म्हणी** (proverbs) and **वाक्प्रचार** (idioms), and dropping one into conversation always gets a smile: **नाचता येईना अंगण वाकडे** (blaming the courtyard for bad dancing), **आपला तो बाब्या, दुसऱ्याचं ते कार्टं** (my child's a darling, yours is a brat — double standards), **दुरून डोंगर साजरे** (hills look lovely from afar — the grass is greener). Matheran, by the way, is a real car-free hill station near Mumbai, and its monkeys really will steal your snacks. Congratulations on finishing the course — आता मराठीत गप्पा मारायला सुरुवात करा!
